extracted.intended_audience: SEC registrants (public companies), corporate counsel, CFOs, corporate secretaries, accountants, and auditors preparing SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and applies the substantive disclosure requirements and instructions from Regulation S-K (Items 305, 307, 308, 401, 402) governing market risk, disclosure controls, internal control over financial reporting, director/officer disclosures, and executive compensation in SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined market risk disclosure permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may present comprehensive market risk disclosures which reflect the combined market risk exposures inherent in both the required and any voluntarily selected instruments, positions, or transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrants choose to present combined exposures they may do so; voluntarily selected instruments included in combined disclosures should be treated consistently with Item 305(a) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular presentation must be consistent with Item 305(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants that choose the tabular presentation disclosure alternative should present voluntarily selected instruments, positions, or transactions in a manner consistent with the requirements in Item 305(a) for market risk sensitive instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabular formats are illustrative; voluntary inclusions must follow the same substantive formatting/contents rules as required items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all of a voluntarily selected instrument type
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant elects to include voluntarily a particular type of instrument, position, or transaction in their quantitative disclosures about market risk, that registrant should include all, rather than some, of those instruments, positions, or transactions within those disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if including a particular commodity position in market risk disclosures, include the entire commodity position, not only a portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality assessment by market risk exposure category
rubrics_metrics.description: A materiality assessment should be made for each market risk exposure category within the trading and other than trading portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess materiality separately for each exposure category; follow instructions in paragraphs 305(a) and 305(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate materiality of fair values outstanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should evaluate the materiality of the fair values of derivative financial instruments, other financial instruments, and derivative commodity instruments outstanding as of the end of the latest fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one prong of the materiality assessment (instruction 5.B.i.). Consider the aggregate fair value exposure as of fiscal year-end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate materiality of potential near-term losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should evaluate the materiality of potential, near-term losses in future earnings, fair values, and/or cash flows from reasonably possible near-term changes in market rates or prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the second prong of the materiality assessment (instruction 5.B.ii.). Consider reasonably possible changes and impacts on earnings/fair value/cash flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose quantitative and qualitative market risk information if material
rubrics_metrics.description: If either the materiality of fair values outstanding or potential near-term losses is material, the registrant should disclose quantitative and qualitative information about market risk for that exposure category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality on either prong triggers disclosure obligations under Item 305(a)/(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not net fair values except as allowed by GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the materiality assessment, registrants generally should not net fair values, except to the extent allowed under generally accepted accounting principles (e.g., FASB ASC Subtopic 210-20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fair value of assets generally should not be netted with fair value of liabilities unless GAAP permits offsetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider magnitude of past market movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should consider the magnitude of past market movements when making the materiality assessment and preparing market risk disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past market movements are one of the factors listed (instruction 5.D.i.) to evaluate exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reasonably possible near-term market movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should consider reasonably possible, near-term market movements when assessing materiality of market risk exposures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corresponds to instruction 5.D.ii.; think forward-looking about plausible market changes over the near term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider potential losses from leverage, option, and multiplier features
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should consider potential losses that may arise from leverage, option, and multiplier features when assessing market risk materiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These product features can magnify losses and should be explicitly considered (instruction 5.D.iii.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'near term' as up to one year
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of these instructions, 'near term' means a period of time going forward up to one year from the date of the financial statements (see FASB ASC Master Glossary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use up-to-one-year horizon for 'near-term' analyses and stress considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'reasonably possible' per GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of these instructions, the term 'reasonably possible' has the same meaning as defined by generally accepted accounting principles (see FASB ASC Master Glossary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the GAAP definition of 'reasonably possible' in judging near-term scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present market risk information outside financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of paragraphs 305(a) and 305(b), registrants should present the information outside of, and not incorporate the information into, the financial statements (including the footnotes to the financial statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants are encouraged to provide required information in one location. Alternative presentation (e.g., inclusion in MD&A) may be used at registrant's discretion but if disclosed in multiple locations, cross-references should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'trading purposes' and 'anticipated transactions'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Trading purposes' means dealing and other trading activities measured at fair value with gains and losses recognized in earnings. 'Anticipated transactions' means transactions (other than transactions involving existing assets or liabilities or transactions necessitated by existing firm commitments) an enterprise expects, but is not obligated, to carry out in the normal course of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions when classifying portfolios and transactions for Item 305 disclosure purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim period disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If interim period financial statements are included or required, discussion and analysis shall be provided to enable the reader to assess sources and effects of material changes in information that would be provided under Item 305 from the end of the preceding fiscal year to the date of the most recent interim balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 305(c) disclosures not required until after first fiscal year end in which Item 305 is applicable; interim MD&A should cover material changes since prior fiscal year-end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory safe harbor applies to Item 305 disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The safe harbor provided in Section 27A of the Securities Act and Section 21E of the Exchange Act shall apply to information provided pursuant to paragraphs (a), (b), and (c) of Item 305 if disclosed by an issuer, person acting on issuer's behalf, outside reviewer retained by issuer making statements on issuer's behalf, or an underwriter with respect to issuer-provided information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of the statutory safe harbors, most information required by certain paragraphs of Item 305 is considered forward-looking statements (with specified historical fact exceptions). The 'meaningful cautionary statements' prong will be satisfied for paragraph (a) if registrant satisfies all requirements of paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller reporting companies exempt from Item 305
rubrics_metrics.description: A smaller reporting company, as defined by §229.10(f)(1), is not required to provide the information required by Item 305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check §229.10(f)(1) for the definition of smaller reporting company to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of Item 305 applicability based on market capitalization and registrant type
rubrics_metrics.description: Bank registrants, thrift registrants, and non-bank/non-thrift registrants with market capitalizations on January 28, 1997 in excess of $2.5 billion should provide Item 305 disclosures in filings that include annual financial statements for fiscal years ending after June 15, 1997; those with market caps $2.5B or less should provide disclosures for fiscal years ending after June 15, 1998.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This instruction sets initial effective dates based on historic measurement date; see General Instruction I.B.1. of Form S-3 for market cap calculation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'bank registrants' and 'control over a depository institution'
rubrics_metrics.description: Bank registrants and thrift registrants include any registrant which has control over a depository institution. A registrant has control if it (i) owns/controls/votes 25%+ of any class of voting securities, (ii) controls the election of a majority of directors/trustees, or (iii) the Federal Reserve or OTS determines registrant exercises controlling influence over management or policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also defines 'depository institution' for these purposes (insured depository institution; institutions accepting demand deposits and making commercial loans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Market capitalization measurement date for Instruction purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For the General Instructions to Item 305, market capitalization is the aggregate market value of common equity as set forth in General Instruction I.B.1. of Form S-3, but measured as of January 28, 1997 instead of the usual 60-day period prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include common equity held by affiliates in the calculation per the instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix examples are illustrative and flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: The tabular examples provided are illustrative of formats that might be used when presenting Item 305 information; registrants are not required to display information in the specific format illustrated. Alternative methods of display are permissible so long as disclosure requirements are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples primarily illustrate possible formats and do not purport to show the full range of instruments; registrants may adapt formats to their instruments and reporting currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose conclusions regarding effectiveness of disclosure controls (Item 307)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose conclusions of the registrant's principal executive and principal financial officers (or persons performing similar functions) regarding the effectiveness of the registrant's disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the period covered by the report, based on the evaluation required by paragraph (b) of §240.13a-15 or §240.15d-15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure must reflect the officers' evaluation under the cited SEC rules; include the as-of date of the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management's annual report on internal control over financial reporting (Item 308(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a report of management on the registrant's internal control over financial reporting that contains specific elements: statement of management's responsibility; identification of framework used; management's assessment of effectiveness (including material weaknesses); and, if applicable, a statement about auditor attestation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must follow the required four elements in paragraph (a)(1)-(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of management responsibility for internal control
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement of management's responsibility for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting for the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first required element of the management report under Item 308(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify framework used to evaluate internal control effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement identifying the framework used by management to evaluate the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting (as required by paragraph (c) of §240.13a-15 or §240.15d-15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the recognized framework used (e.g., COSO) as part of the management report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management's assessment of effectiveness and material weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Management's assessment of the effectiveness of internal control as of the end of the most recent fiscal year, including a statement whether internal control is effective and disclosure of any material weakness identified. Management cannot conclude that internal control is effective if there are one or more material weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material weaknesses exist they must be disclosed and management must not claim overall effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement regarding auditor's attestation on internal control (when applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is an accelerated filer or large accelerated filer (or otherwise includes an attestation report in its annual report), include a statement that the registered public accounting firm that audited the financial statements has issued an attestation report on the registrant's internal control over financial reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Item 308(a)(4) — include the auditor's attestation statement when required by filer status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation report requirement for accelerated/large accelerated filers (Item 308(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant (other than an emerging growth company) is an accelerated filer or a large accelerated filer, provide the registered public accounting firm's attestation report on internal control over financial reporting in the annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emerging growth companies are excluded from this attestation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose changes in internal control that materially affect controls (Item 308(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any change in internal control over financial reporting identified in connection with the required evaluation that occurred during the registrant's last fiscal quarter that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the registrant's internal control over financial reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For annual reports, consider changes identified during the fourth fiscal quarter; disclose material changes or those reasonably likely to be material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain evidential matter supporting management's assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must maintain evidential matter, including documentation, to provide reasonable support for management's assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document controls, testing, and evidence used to form the assessment (Instruction 2 to Item 308).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of directors (Item 401(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: List the names and ages of all directors and all persons nominated or chosen to become directors; indicate positions/offices with the registrant, term of office, any periods served, and briefly describe any arrangement or understanding between the person and others pursuant to which he was or is to be selected as a director or nominee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include arrangements with directors/officers acting solely in their capacities as such; ensure nominees have consented; proxy-specific instructions apply (Instructions 1–5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of executive officers (Item 401(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: List names and ages of all executive officers and persons chosen to become executive officers; indicate positions/offices, term of office, period served, and briefly describe any arrangement or understanding for selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include arrangements solely in their capacities as such; persons chosen must consent to serve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of significant non-executive employees (Item 401(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify persons (e.g., production managers, sales managers, research scientists) who are not executive officers but make or are expected to make significant contributions to the business, and disclose their background to the same extent as for executive officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure need not be made if the registrant was reporting under Section 13(a) or 15(d) or exempt immediately prior to the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family relationships disclosure (Item 401(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: State the nature of any family relationship between any director, executive officer, or person nominated or chosen to become a director or executive officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction defines 'family relationship' as any relationship by blood, marriage, or adoption not more remote than first cousin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business experience disclosure (Item 401(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe the business experience during the past five years of each director, executive officer, nominee, and significant employee, including principal occupations and employment, the name and principal business of organizations, whether such organization is a parent/subsidiary/affiliate, and, for directors, the specific experience/qualifications that support the conclusion they should serve as a director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material, coverage may extend beyond five years; when employed less than five years provide explanation of prior responsibilities to adequately disclose prior experience; focus on information showing level of professional competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directorships disclosure (Item 401(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate any other directorships held by each director or nominee during the past five years, including companies with securities registered under Section 12 or subject to Section 15(d) or registered investment companies; registrant may identify a 'fund complex' and provide number of investment company directorships instead of listing each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the fund complex alternative where applicable to simplify disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involvement in certain legal proceedings (Item 401(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe events during the past ten years material to evaluation of ability or integrity of any director, nominee, or executive officer, including bankruptcy petitions, criminal convictions or pending proceedings, injunctions/orders limiting activities, suspensions by authorities, civil findings of securities/commodities law violations, judicial/administrative orders relating to violations of securities/commodities/financial institution laws, or sanctions by self-regulatory organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item enumerates eight categories (f)(1)-(8). Excludes traffic/other minor offenses. See Instructions to paragraph (f) for computation and disclosure details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute ten-year period and permitted omissions/mitigations (Instructions to 401(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For computing the ten-year period, use the date of final order/judgment/decree or bankruptcy filing as specified; if an event has occurred and information is omitted on grounds of non-materiality, the registrant may furnish supplemental materials to the Commission at time of filing; registrant may explain mitigating circumstances; certain proxy presentation exceptions apply; paragraph (f)(7) does not apply to private litigant settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified computation dates and allowed procedures for omitted information and mitigating explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoters and control persons disclosure (Item 401(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants not previously subject to Section 13(a)/15(d) reporting for the prior 12 months and that had a promoter in the past five fiscal years must describe for any promoter events enumerated in (f)(1)-(f)(6) that occurred during past five years that are material to a voting or investment decision; similarly describe events for any control person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions to paragraph (f) apply; paragraph (g) does not apply to subsidiaries that have been reporting for prior 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy/Form 10-K cross-reference instruction for executive officer information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information regarding executive officers called for by Item 401 need not be furnished in proxy or information statements prepared under Schedule 14A or 14C if relying on General Instruction G of Form 10-K; such information would instead be furnished in a section captioned 'Information about our Executive Officers' in Part I of Form 10-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form 10-K cross-reference where permitted to avoid duplication in proxy materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign private issuers for Item 402
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign private issuer will be deemed to comply with Item 402 if it provides the information required by Items 6.B, 6.E.2, and 6.F of Form 20-F, with more detailed information if publicly available or required by home jurisdiction or market rules, or paragraph (19) of General Instruction B of Form 40-F, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign private issuers may provide domestic Item 402 disclosure but must provide Item 402(w) in annual report or registration statement where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: All compensation covered (Item 402(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 402 requires clear, concise, and understandable disclosure of all plan and non-plan compensation awarded to, earned by, or paid to the named executive officers and directors by any person for all services rendered in all capacities to the registrant and its subsidiaries, unless specifically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all such compensation even if required elsewhere; amounts reported for one fiscal year may be required to be reported differently for another year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons covered — named executive officers (Item 402(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure shall be provided for: (i) the principal executive officer (PEO); (ii) the principal financial officer (PFO); (iii) the registrant's three most highly compensated executive officers other than the PEO and PFO who were serving at end of last fiscal year; and (iv) up to two additional individuals who would have been included under (iii) but were not serving as executive officers at the end of the last fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These individuals are the 'named executive officers' for whom compensation disclosure is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of most highly compensated executive officers (Instruction to 402(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the most highly compensated executive officers by reference to total compensation for the last completed fiscal year (as required to be disclosed pursuant to Item 402(c)(2)(x)) reduced by amounts required to be disclosed pursuant to Item 402(c)(2)(viii); however, no disclosure need be provided for any executive officer other than the PEO and PFO whose total compensation, as so reduced, does not exceed $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the reduction and $100,000 exclusion when determining which officers to include under Item 402(a)(3)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of subsidiary executive officers may be appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be appropriate for a registrant to include as named executive officers one or more executive officers or other employees of subsidiaries in the disclosure required by Item 402.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider materiality and relevance of subsidiary officers' roles when deciding inclusion.
